title: Chapter 2 Quiz 6
description: A mixed review of Chapter 2. Say how sure you are before you check.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: A program checks whether a number is positive and prints a different message in each case. Which type of algorithm is this?
questions.explanation: A decision between two outcomes: conditional. Watch out: printing a message is linear, but choosing between two messages is a decision.

questions.question: Summing all the elements of an array is a task for an…
questions.explanation: We repeat the same addition for every element: a loop. Watch out: it can be written recursively, but the natural family is iterative.

questions.question: Exploring every folder inside other folders is best described by a…
questions.explanation: Each folder contains the same kind of problem, only smaller. Watch out: looping over one flat list is iterative, but nested folders call for recursion.

questions.question: Match each term to its meaning.
right: Makes the locally optimal choice at each step
Finds the position of an element
questions.explanation: A review of the families and approaches. Watch out: top-down and bottom-up are opposite directions.

questions.question: Which of these are **design approaches**?
questions.explanation: Top-down and bottom-up are design approaches. Watch out: greedy and sorting describe kinds of algorithm, not ways of designing.

questions.question: A recursive algorithm solves a problem by repeating a loop.
questions.explanation: Recursion solves a problem by calling itself on smaller sub-problems. Watch out: loops repeat too, but they belong to iterative algorithms.

questions.assertion: Merge sort is a divide and conquer algorithm.
questions.reason: It splits the data into smaller parts, sorts them and combines the results.
questions.explanation: Both are true and the reason explains why merge sort is divide and conquer. Watch out: merge sort is also a sorting algorithm, and both labels hold.

questions.question: This algorithm should display Adult for people who are 18 or older, and Minor otherwise. One line has an error.
questions.code:
Read(age)
If age < 18 Then
    Display("Adult")
Else
    Display("Minor")
EndIf
questions.explanation: The test is reversed: people under 18 would be called Adult. Watch out: the displayed words look right, only the comparison is wrong.

questions.question: In the Fibonacci sequence F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1 and F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2). What is F(6)?
questions.explanation: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8: F(6) = 8. Watch out: the sequence starts at F(0) = 0, so F(6) is the seventh term.

questions.question: Which approach solves the simplest sub-problems first and then combines them?
questions.explanation: Bottom-up builds the answer from the smallest pieces. Watch out: top-down also deals with sub-problems, but it starts from the whole.
